name: Trollface
blurb: A smug, grinning MS Paint face from 2008, the symbol of internet trolling
title: Trollface Meme: Meaning, Origin & Who Drew It
description: Trollface is a grinning cartoon face drawn in MS Paint by Carlos Ramirez and posted on DeviantArt on 19 September 2008, later the face of trolling.
answer: Trollface is a black-and-white cartoon face with a wide, smug, mischievous grin, used to show that someone is trolling: pranking or baiting others for fun. Carlos Ramirez, then an 18-year-old college student in Oakland, drew it in MS Paint for a rage comic and posted it on his DeviantArt page on 19 September 2008. It took off on 4chan that year and became one of the most recognisable faces of early-2010s rage comics, usually captioned "Problem?".

body: It is a wide, slightly lumpy face drawn in rough black lines, with narrowed eyes, raised cheeks and an enormous toothy grin stretching almost ear to ear. The expression says "I know exactly what I just did to you, and I'm enjoying it."
In rage comics, the Trollface character usually appears in the last panel after tricking someone, often with the one-word caption "Problem?" or "U mad?".

head: Date
Event
rows: Carlos Ramirez (DeviantArt user Whynne) posts the MS Paint comic "Trolls" with the face on 19 September.
Ramirez posts the image to 4chan, where it quickly becomes popular.
Trollface spreads to Reddit and becomes a rage-comic staple.
Ramirez registers the comic with the U.S. Copyright Office.
A Wii U game called Meme Run is removed from Nintendo's store over unlicensed use of Trollface; in April Kotaku reports Ramirez has earned over $100,000 from licensing.

ul: Rage comics: the troll pulls a prank, then grins in the last panel.
Replying with just the face after a successful joke or bait-and-switch.
Captions "Problem?" and "U mad?", the classic Trollface lines.
Trollge: a dark, unsmiling Trollface half hidden in shadow, popular since late 2020 in eerie "incident" story memes.

body: It is also used as shorthand for trolling in general, as in "that reply is pure Trollface energy".

Trollface is a classic from the rage-comic era. It is less common in everyday memes than in 2010 to 2012, but everyone who was online then recognises it, and newer ironic and horror-themed edits keep it alive. It is also a rare meme with a clear owner: Ramirez holds the copyright and has licensed it for games, shirts and other products, and has acted against unlicensed commercial uses.

faq.a: Carlos Ramirez, who drew it in MS Paint and posted it on DeviantArt under the name Whynne on 19 September 2008.
It is the troll's smug question after a prank: "Got a problem with that?" It mocks the person who fell for the joke.
Yes. Ramirez registered the comic with the U.S. Copyright Office in 2010 and has earned licensing income from it.
